The Trinity: Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
Contributions. ❶Capability-driven multimodal RSI. We make shared capability requirements
the organizing principle of Harness evolution. Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real turns these re-
quirements into compact training worlds, yielding a reusable module-based Harness tree whose
specialization motivates capability-aware routing.❷Capability–module priors for Harness design.
We connect task-level capability requirements to reusable module configurations, using empirical
associations and controlled interventions to examine which module support matters for a task.❸
Efficient evolution and transfer.We show that targeting shared decision logic supports effective
Harness improvement at low evolution cost, with transfer across heterogeneous tasks, unseen
benchmarks, and real-world embodied settings.
2. Preliminaries
2.1. Multimodal Agentic Tasks
Long-horizon multimodal agentic tasks span interactive games [38], GUI manipulation [39], and
embodied interaction [13, 14]. They combine perception, understanding, reasoning, and generation
with memory, planning, and adaptation across observation–action sequences. Agents must retain
evidence, revise hypotheses, and adjust plans as observations arrive. Because later decisions
depend on earlier actions and feedback, misread observations or forgotten constraints can propagate
across steps. Agent performance thus increasingly depends on effective Harness organization
and coordination. Dynamically coordinating capabilities over long interactions and adapting to
increasingly large, heterogeneous task sets remain key challenges.

Perceptionextracts facts 𝑓𝑡;Memorybuilds a history-conditioned view 𝑣𝑡;Inferencemaintains
compatible candidates;Planningranks or prunes options into directive𝑑𝑡;Orchestrationidentifies
applicable resources; andLoopresolves execution 𝑒𝑡 and commitment𝑐𝑡, including withholding
action. These roles are independent of task categories and capability-tree nodes. The equations
describe functional roles and their data dependencies; individual module bindings are invoked under
the runtime policy described in Section 3.4.
Modules are pure functions of supplied public records, without hidden-state access or environment
actions. Only Memory may declare explicitcarry; hypothesis refutation requires observed contra-
diction. All protocols may emit typed readiness signals, while Loop resolves execution. Orchestration
assesses applicability, relevance, and trust within a fixed host-exposed tool set. Evolution updates
module configurations with𝜃fixed.
Capabilities and protocols have a many-to-many relationship: the tree groups shared requirements,
while protocols locate module updates. Hypothesis consistency can involve Memory organizing
evidence, Inference checking compatibility, and Planning ranking informative tests; the same Memory
module can support several requirements. Explorer retains node modules; Creator uses the same
tree structure and consolidates its next Base Harness. Evaluation-time skills are prepared separately
(Section 4.1); they are not stored, evolved, inherited, or routed in the tree.
